conflicts.note: Kept 480 hp, Ford's standard GT rating. 486 hp is Ford's figure for a GT with the optional active-valve performance exhaust (Ford newsroom, Jalopnik, MotorWeek, The Drive headlines quote it as 'the' GT figure). Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

Kept 7,150 rpm from Ford's 2026 technical spec sheet (7,250 rpm with the active exhaust). MustangSpecs.com lists 480 hp @ 7,500 rpm, the figure elsewhere tied to the Dark Horse's redline. No 2024 Ford sheet figure was seen. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

Kept 415 lb-ft to match the standard 480 hp rating (Jalopnik reporting Ford, TFLcar, cars.com, Ford Performance crate-engine page). 418 lb-ft applies only with the optional active-valve exhaust and is the only torque figure Ford's newsroom summary printed. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

Kept 3,730 lb, the only maker figure naming the GT fastback manual, but it is a preliminary estimate (Ford sheet dated Sept. 14, 2022; automatic 3,752 lb). 3,741 lb 'base curb weight' (Cars.com, CarBuzz, iSeeCars, Motor Matchup, Auto123; transmission not stated; likely one licensed data feed; exactly the midpoint of Ford's manual and automatic estimates). 3,827 lb (Yahoo Autos / The Drive first drive, Motor1 for a GT Premium; one summary pairs it with the 6-speed manual). 3,866 lb (Edmunds test car, GT Performance Package manual; the earlier summary did not give the page, so it is not recorded as testWeightLb). 3,947 lb (MotorBiscuit, said to be the manual; Road Blazing, GT Premium). 3,933 lb (AutoPadre, GT Premium) also appeared. European 446 hp GT figures (about 1,733 kg) are a different market. A modeller should treat curb weight as uncertain by up to about 200 lb. This run: Motor Matchup's 2026 GT Fastback Manual listing gives 3,731 lb (different model year), and the Edmunds Performance Package manual test car's 3,866 lb is now recorded as testWeightLb from Edmunds' Dark Horse test table. Second reader: CJ Pony Parts' S650 vs S550 curb-weight comparison lists the 2024 'Mustang GT Base' at 3,740 lb (transmission not stated); LMR's scale weigh-in of a GT with the 400A package and Brembo brakes was summarised as 3,843 lb (presumably the automatic car behind the weightDistFrontPct figure); Cars.com-type listings again showed 3,741 lb. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

Kept 55% front (a weigh-in of an automatic GT reported by Motor1; Motor Matchup's 2026 GT Fastback Manual listing). The second reader's search found only 53% front on a video-game data page (not a measurement) and an article's 'nearly 50:50' that described an eight-speed transaxle, i.e. not this car; neither was used. No measured split for a 2024 manual GT surfaced. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

Kept 62.0 in (Ford's preliminary 2024 sheet, GT column). Ford's 2026 sheet gives 62.4 in for the GT; CarExpert NZ gives 62.2 in, which the summary said matches the Dark Horse column of the 2024 sheet. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.
Kept 64.7 in (Ford's preliminary 2024 sheet). Ford's 2026 sheet gives 64.9 in; CarExpert NZ 63.9 in (said to match the Dark Horse column). Read from search-result summary; page not opened.
Kept 55.0 in (Ford's preliminary 2024 sheet, GT column). CarExpert NZ gives 55.7 in. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

Not recorded. 5.3 in came from a single unnamed review in a search summary; 143 mm (about 5.6 in, listed as '6 in') is CarsGuide's figure for the Australian-market GT with the 10-speed automatic; Autopadre's 5.2 to 5.7 in range mixed in Mach-E entries. Cars.com showed no figure for the GT and Ford's spec-sheet summaries did not show one. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

Not recorded. 7,200 rpm comes only from 2022 (S550) GT manual owners on a forum; 7,500 rpm is the Dark Horse's redline (Fox News). No 2024 GT figure surfaced. Second reader: a targeted search again returned only the Dark Horse's 7,500-rpm redline and no GT figure. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

Second reader corrected the kept text to plain 'limited-slip'. Ford's 2026 Mustang sheet was summarised as '3.55 limited-slip; 3.73 TORSEN limited-slip' (the Torsen comes with the Performance Package's 3.73 axle). 'Electronic limited slip rear differential' for the 3.55 axle appears only in Roadblazing's spec box for a GT Premium review; Ford's wording has no 'electronic', so on this evidence the base axle should not be modelled as an electronically controlled differential. No 2024 Ford wording was seen. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

Kept 255/45R18 square for the base GT (iSeeCars, Mavis, Goodyear, Firestone). 255/40R19 and the staggered 255/40R19 / 275/40R19 set appear in Goodyear's and Michelin's GT fitment lists and were judged to be GT Premium or Performance Package fitments; the Edmunds test car had the Performance Package. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

Not recorded. A Mustang7G forum post cites Cd 0.37 for the 2024 Mustang ('basically the same as the prior model') with no source. Ford claims the lowest drag of any Mustang but gave no number in any summary. No frontal area appeared. Second reader: a targeted search found no Cd or frontal area; one engineering article was summarised as saying Ford claims overall drag force reduced by 3% without giving a Cd (the summary did not say which Mustang generation it describes). Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

Kept Auto123's 37.8 ft curb-to-curb (also on a dealer-style GT listing). cars-data.com gives 12.2 m (40.0 ft), possibly wall-to-wall or a different market. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.
Kept Auto123's 13.8 in. TrueCar's 2022 (S550) GT Fastback lists 13.9 in; Cars.com shows 14 in but the layout left the axle unclear. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

Not recorded. TrueCar's 2022 (S550) GT Fastback lists 13.0 in rear (different generation); Cars.com's 2024 page shows 14 in with the axle unclear. No 2024 figure could be tied to the rear axle. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

Kept 155 mph governed (MotorBiscuit spec table; Road Blazing GT Premium spec box; a mustang7g forum post saying the governor is 155 on the GT and 168 on the Dark Horse). Others: 'will top 150 mph' (The Auto Channel review of a manual GT coupe), an estimated 160 mph (Motor1), 145 and about 140 mph limiters (forum posts), 175 mph (Motor Matchup simulation), and 168 mph in an unlabeled KBB column that appears to be the Dark Horse. No Ford or measured figure. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

Kept 18 mpg from fueleconomy.gov record 47558 (5.0L 6-speed manual). AutoPadre lists 19. CJ Pony Parts' 15/24/17 appears to be the automatic, and Ford Authority's 14 mpg city is the Dark Horse manual. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

Kept Edmunds' 4.8 s (Performance Package manual GT hardtop) because Edmunds has the most figures for this engine/transmission/drive (0-60, quarter mile and trap, 60-0, skidpad, test weight) and they were read on Edmunds' own pages. Car and Driver 4.2 s and 12.5 s @ 114 mph for 'the GT 6-speed' (relayed by a J.D. Power page and a reposted October 2023 issue; options not stated; MotorBiscuit repeats 4.2 s manual). MotorTrend 4.3 s and 12.5 s @ 114.7 mph (manual GT WITH Performance Package and active exhaust; forum repost of a comparison test). Both of those likely use a one-foot rollout, which may explain part of the 0.5 s gap; Edmunds' convention was not stated. Consumer Reports 4.6 s (transmission not stated); The Auto Channel about 4.0 s (not clearly instrumented). The 5.6 s once read as Edmunds' GT is its EcoBoost convertible (14.2 s @ 95 mph). Second reader: Edmunds was summarised as saying it 'doesn't use rollout in any of its reported 0-60-mph times' (testRollout false), which accounts for part of the gap to the other testers' figures; The Auto Channel's review was re-summarised as 0-60 in 4 seconds and a quarter mile of 12.5 seconds at 115 mph, and J.D. Power again relayed Car and Driver's 4.2 s and 12.5 s for 'the GT 6-speed'. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

Kept Edmunds' 12.7 s @ 111.6 mph (same test as the other kept figures). Car and Driver 12.5 s @ 114 mph (second-hand, options not stated) and MotorTrend 12.5 s @ 114.7 mph (forum repost; Performance Package and active exhaust manual) were not kept; see testQuarterMileMph. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

Kept Edmunds' 111.6 mph. Car and Driver 114 mph (reposted October 2023 issue) and MotorTrend 114.7 mph (forum repost). The roughly 3 mph trap-speed gap is large for the same rated engine; a modeller should not tune power to Edmunds' trap alone. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

Kept 103 ft from Edmunds' test table for the Performance Package manual GT. A second Edmunds page says the EcoBoost's 105 ft was '3 feet more than the hardtop GT', implying 102 ft. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.
